properties.bedrock_type: Carboniferous Sandstone and Siltstone (Inverclyde and Strathclyde Groups)
properties.mineralogy: Quartz arenite, feldspathic sandstone, carbonaceous shale, and glacial till overburden
properties.drainage: Northward subterranean fall towards the Water of Leith basin and Firth of Forth

properties.primary_surfacing: Coarsely textured bituminous asphalt carriage roadway bordered by dressed Scottish whinstone and Craigleith sandstone kerbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Polished pedestrian flagstone pavements with faint longitudinal rain-channeling and sunken service access covers
properties.micro_grading: Steep steady northward downward gradient plunging through the New Town street grid towards Stockbridge

properties.groundcover: Cultivated private basement area planters and lower valley woodland canopies framing St Stephen's Church

properties.primary_building_typology: Late 18th-century Georgian New Town classical terraced tenements and neoclassical civic church terminus

structures.name: West Terrace (Frederick Street Even Nos, including 44-46 Frederick St)
structures.roof_geometry: Pitched Scottish slate with canted lead-clad dormers and substantial mutual stone chimney stacks with terracotta pots
structures.facade_material: Droved and polished Craigleith cream ashlar sandstone with ground-floor built-out shopfronts and rusticated basements
structures.weathering_patina: Pronounced atmospheric carbon crusting and soot darkening across cornice reveals, string courses, and sandstone ashlar quoins

structures.name: East Terrace (Frederick Street Odd Nos)
structures.roof_geometry: Pitched slate roof with regular dormer windows and rectilinear stone coped skews
structures.facade_material: Blonde ashlar sandstone with timber sash-and-case fenestration and cast-iron basement lightwell railings
structures.weathering_patina: Differential grey-buff weathering, iron-stain wash under sills, and historic soot deposition

structures.name: St Stephen's Church (Stockbridge Vista Terminus)
structures.roof_geometry: Monumental square neoclassical clock tower terminating in a balustraded stone crown
structures.facade_material: Massive dressed blonde freestone ashlar with deep arched portals and classical pilasters
structures.weathering_patina: Subtle silvery-grey atmospheric weathering across elevated ashlar balustrades and rusticated plinths

properties.lighting_condition: Delighted Scottish Northern Daylight with crisp raking shadows delineating classical cornices and distant Firth of Forth horizon
